newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Vodacom meets one bln rand licence rule.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Vodacom meets one bln rand licence rule.

text.p: South African mobile phone operator Vodacom said on Tuesday that it met a one billion rand economic development condition in its operating licence seven years ahead of schedule.

Vodacom, a joint-venture between Britain's Vodafone Plc, Rembrandt Group Ltd and Telkom, had agreed to the 10-year Joint Economic Development (JED) project in the terms of its original licence granted late in 1993.

JED compelled the firm to generate one billion rands worth of economic activity outside its normal operations over the next 10 years. Failure to do so would have resulted in heavy financial penalties.

Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said the rapid growth of South Africa's cellular phone industry had allowed the conditions to be met in just three years and the firm would now take on new targets from the telecommunications ministry.
"Our JED programme does not stop here. We are committed to continue supporting government's macro-economic objectives," he said.

Vodacom has more than 640,000 subscribers, giving it about 60 percent of the South African market. The industry, which is barely three years old, has already attracted more than a million mobile phones users.

The JED programme covers a wide range of activities from attracting foreign investment, subsidised community phones for disadvantaged settlements and sponsoring students through training and university.

The individual projects were assessed by a JED committee and given a rand credit valuation. Knott-Craig said 1.046 billion rands worth of credits had been generated so far in JED with up to another 140 million rands worth still being evaluated.
